content.title: Quiz: Spotting Invoice and Payment-Redirect Fraud
content.summary: Test your ability to spot payment redirect fraud, fake invoices, and unauthorized banking changes with this 5-question Finance quiz.
content.body_markdown: Building on our earlier debrief on 'Invoice and Payment-Redirect Fraud' and our 'Scanning Safely' quishing module [ORG], this quiz helps our Finance team spot fraudulent payment requests. Scammers often spoof email addresses, craft fake invoices [S1, S3], or manipulate approval workflows to misdirect payouts [S7, S8]. We all get tricked sometimes, so test your knowledge below to help keep Nebulon safe!
key_points: Always verify banking detail changes out-of-band using trusted phone numbers [ORG].
Scammers use slight variations in email addresses to spoof trusted contacts [S1].
Unusual urgency and unexpected invoice modifications are major warning signs of billing fraud [S1, S3].
Report suspicious payment requests immediately to security@nebulon.example.com [ORG].
red_flags: Slightly altered email domain names or sender addresses [S1]
Urgent requests to bypass standard financial verification procedures [S1, S7]
Unexpected requests to update vendor payout bank account details [S1, S3]
Links directing you to external sites to sign payment policy acknowledgements [S3]
actions: Verify bank detail changes using established, out-of-band communication channels [ORG].
Check sender email addresses carefully for subtle typos [S1].
Report suspicious invoice or payment emails to security@nebulon.example.com [ORG].
content.report_how: Forward any suspicious payment emails or requests to security@nebulon.example.com or use the Report Phish button [ORG].

quiz.question: A long-time vendor emails an urgent request to update their banking details before an upcoming payout, attaching an updated invoice. What is the safest action?
options: Update the banking details immediately so the payment deadline is not missed.
Reply directly to the email to confirm if the new banking details are correct.
Verify the request by calling the vendor using a trusted phone number already on file.
Forward the email to a team member to approve the payment.
quiz.explanation: Attackers frequently send fake invoices or spoof vendor emails to alter payout accounts [S1, S3]. Always verify bank detail updates using trusted out-of-band channels [ORG].
quiz.targets_mistake: Falls for 'Finance/AP/vendor billing' phishing (missed 15 of 48 phishing emails) MITRE T1566

quiz.question: You receive an urgent message formatted as an executive announcement requesting an immediate wire transfer for a confidential vendor deal. What should you do?
options: Process the wire transfer immediately as instructed by executive leadership.
Pause and verify the payment request through standard internal approval procedures.
Reply to the email asking the executive to send their password.
Forward the email to your personal account to review later.
quiz.explanation: Scammers spoof executive communications and misuse internal approval processes to push through unauthorized payments [S1, S7, S8]. Always follow standard verification steps.
quiz.targets_mistake: Falls for 'Corporate communications / executive announcements' phishing (missed 4 of 12 phishing emails) MITRE T1566

quiz.question: An email asks you to urgently click a link to sign a mandatory 'Vendor Billing Compliance Policy' survey. What is the primary red flag?
options: It asks you to complete an unexpected survey link to confirm financial or policy details.
It comes from your internal IT service desk.
It gives you two weeks to read a policy document.
It contains no clickable links or attachments.
quiz.explanation: Phishing emails often claim there is a policy issue or require you to confirm details via external links [S3]. Scammers exploit compliance themes to steal credentials or alter payment records [S7, S8].
quiz.targets_mistake: Falls for 'Compliance/policy acknowledgements & surveys' phishing (missed 9 of 30 phishing emails) MITRE T1566

quiz.question: An external message claiming to be a data privacy auditor asks for a file containing sensitive vendor payment records. How should you respond?
options: Send the requested vendor records right away to comply with the audit.
Reply asking the sender for their auditor ID card number.
Refuse to send sensitive records and report the email to security@nebulon.example.com.
Upload the records to a public file sharing folder.
quiz.explanation: Scammers send phishing emails targeting sensitive data to gather intel for future business payment scams [S1, S3]. Always report requests for sensitive records to security@nebulon.example.com [ORG].
quiz.targets_mistake: Falls for 'Data privacy / records management' phishing (missed 6 of 18 phishing emails) MITRE T1566

quiz.question: Which tactic do cybercriminals commonly use to make fraudulent vendor payment emails appear legitimate?
options: Sending emails only on official public holidays.
Spoofing email addresses with subtle variations, such as john.kelly@examplecompany.com versus john.kelley@examplecompany.com.
Attaching official government stamps to every fake invoice.
Requesting payment exclusively in cash by postal mail.
quiz.explanation: Scammers frequently spoof email accounts with slight spelling changes to trick victims into believing fraudulent messages are authentic [S1].
